title: Gradients: linear, radial, conic, repeating
learningObjectives: Explain gradients: linear, radial, conic, repeating and apply the visual effect with a usable fallback.

understand.concept: CSS gradients are generated images. linear-gradient() transitions along a line, radial-gradient() spreads from a centre, conic-gradient() sweeps around a centre, and repeating variants repeat their colour-stop pattern.
understand.whyItMatters: Gradients can communicate grouping or create decorative surfaces without image downloads. Keep text contrast adequate and avoid using gradients as the only carrier of information.
understand.analogy: Different gradients are different paths for a colour transition: straight, outward from a centre, around a centre, or repeated.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual painting, clipping, and media behaviour follow CSS rendering rules.

explain.narrative: Each card demonstrates a different gradient geometry. Add a repeating-linear-gradient to create a striped pattern.

examples.explanation: Each card demonstrates a different gradient geometry. Add a repeating-linear-gradient to create a striped pattern.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered visual example demonstrating the CSS effect.

practise.guidedTask: Create four swatches using linear, radial, conic, and repeating gradients. Check text contrast on each.
practise.independentTask: Create a decorative component using this effect. Test readability, responsive sizing, and a baseline appearance when the effect is unavailable.
hints: Keep important information in semantic HTML.
Test the effect on different sizes and backgrounds.
Do not let decorative effects obscure focus or text.

options: Readable content and a usable fallback

questions.explanation: Decorative effects should enhance content rather than become the only way to access it.
